problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨4{t}^{3},\,-2{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=1.$ Do not round the answers.

$a(1)=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Velocity Vector
examples.problem:
The velocity vector $\mathbf{v} = \langle u, v \rangle,$ measured in $\textrm{m}/\textrm s,$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds, is given by

$$
\mathbf{v} = \langle t^4-t^2, 2t^3\rangle.
$$

Find the acceleration vector and the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
examples.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3}-2t,\,6{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨4(1)^{3}-2(1),6(1)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|\mathbf a(1)|\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨2,6⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{40} \\  & =2\sqrt{10}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨4{t}^{2},\,-\frac{3}{32}{t}^{4}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{3}{32}{t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨8t,\,-\frac{3}{8}{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
